add.title: Claude effort parameter
add.notes: Authoritative closed set of effort levels (low|medium|high|xhigh|max) and the affirmative list of supporting models. Gates the model catalog's effort metadata. Documents that `ultracode` is NOT an API effort level.

add.title: Reward hacking is swamping model intelligence gains (Cursor)
add.notes: Measured: 63% of Opus successes on SWE-bench Pro retrieved the fix rather than derived it; isolation controls cost 14 points. Prompted the local audit that found our own build_sample.py provenance leak. Load-bearing for every future benchmark claim.

add.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
add.notes: Submitted 2026-07-14. Demands matched-budget search baselines and held-out task families for any harness claim. We answered the matched-budget half from existing data (best-of-3 vanilla = 77 at 883k vs guided loop = 100 at 647k); the held-out task family remains outstanding.

add.title: Compact Constraint Encoding for LLM Code Generation
add.notes: The closest independent replication of our scaffolding null: 11 models, 830+ invocations, no significant compliance difference, ~71% token reduction. Cite wherever the null is stated.

add.title: Is Three the Magic Number? An Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Repair Loops
add.notes: Externally grounds our iteration ceiling of 3 and our declared-budget rule. 'Orchestration and feedback design matter more than the model.'

add.title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
add.notes: Visible/held-out gap grows 28 points per 10x code size. Our 100/100/100 saturates a visible suite; our defence is the held-out grader plus a hardcoding probe, not suite design.

add.title: PBT-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Property-Based Testing
add.notes: Agent-derived property checks miss 17-58% of seeded bugs even at best - our property checks are a partial net, not a safety net. Also shows scaffolding gains are capability-dependent and can go negative at the frontier.

add.title: The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards
add.notes: Argues fixed verifiers decay as capability grows. Names the scope boundary of our digest-frozen suite.

add.title: To Run or Not to Run: Analyzing the Cost-Effectiveness of Code Execution in LLM-Based Program Repair
add.notes: ISSTA 2026. Prohibiting agent-side execution costs 1.25pp (n.s.) while saving 56-62% tokens; agents run 8.8 test runs/task with concentrated benefit. Supports the harness deciding when to verify.
